## TASK-009 - Add one selected adoption route for earlier projects

Extend the existing prepare-existing workflow with --adopt-module curator and explicit --refresh-module curator for an earlier Curator installation; retain project-curator aliases. With no prior Curator selection, adoption chooses the reviewed integrated edition. With prior completed selection, ordinary adoption/rerun verifies that recorded edition; only explicit refresh chooses the new source/recipe inventory. One selected operation coordinates project wiring and the current ontology-owner transaction, links the resulting immutable receipt and archives prior receipt bytes by hash. Missing baseline ontology is a recorded neutral prerequisite; custom/incomplete/legacy conflicts are preserved and diagnosed.

### Risks

- Do not execute arbitrary copied project helpers to manufacture semantic readiness; permit only reviewed source validators or data-only parsing.

### Acceptance criteria

- File-only Curator installation or one capability name fails integrated readiness. Selected required failures retain a partial verification stage/nonzero result; preserved custom gaps retain degraded diagnostics.
- Static assessment carries exact edition, source/destination inventory hashes and blocked dependency/owner next action without executing unknown destination Python.
- Runtime remains not-exercised and publication not authorized by assessment even when every static integrated check passes.
- Neutral Template completeness validates the complete recipe and future destination inputs with active graphs empty, publication unbound and session disabled. Source-current declaration remains separate from installed, configured, authorized, compatible, pending, completed and runtime-observed claims.

### Planned verification

- Delete or corrupt one function, binding, source locator, owner entry, graph config selection and dependency resource in separate fixtures; each produces a named non-ready result.
- Test disabled-but-compatible choice versus missing required capability without conflating either with runtime evidence.

### Risks

- No blind rollback, hand-edited receipt, abandoned-lock inference or wholesale replacement may clear a failure.

### Acceptance criteria

- Faults at every newly added durable stage retain attributable partial evidence and preserve unrelated data.
- Identical retry completes or verifies once; changed recipe/helper/source, destination edit, identity, opt-out, active owner or selection refuses replay without deleting history.
- Canonical ontology completion must precede selected integrated setup completion; completed receipt is never used to overwrite later project edits.
- Recovery preserves session-disabled, capture-off and publication-disabled choices, old licensing/roles/Task/memory/ontology records and current owner checks at every durable stage; no reset of session usage or expiry evasion can permit replay.

### Planned verification

- Inject faults before/after integration config and graph publication, receipt linkage, registration and static verification.
- Run unchanged retry twice; compare capabilities/bindings/registrations and original receipt history; run stale-source, changed-target, concurrent writer, symlink/hardlink and unknown-file negative controls.
